 Hon'Ble Mr Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge

The appellant/applicant is dealer of Maruti Suzuki Vehicles.

02. In the course of its dealership business, the vehicles to be sold in the market are transported without bearing registration number by engagement by the appellant/applicant of drivers who are in its employment, contractual or otherwise.
03. One of said vehicle being sent from Jammu to Srinagar was a Maruti 800 Car bearing Chassis No. 2860044 driven by the respondent No. 2- Gurmeet Singh.

04. On 7th July, 2012, the said vehicle was engaged in an accident which resulted in death of accident victim Mohd Shafi Khanday leading to registration of FIR No. 96 of 2012 by the Police Station Qazigund.
05.

The dependents of said deceased Mohammad Shafi Khanday i.e. widow-Mst Noora Begum,
son-Firdous Ahmad and father-Gh. Qadir preferred a claim petition on File No. 07/CP on 24th July,
2024 before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pulwama, in which the driver, the Peaks Auto Pvt. Ltd Through Its vs National Insurance Company Through Its on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165160875/
1 appellant/applicant, as being the owner and the insurer respondent no. 1-National Insurance Company came to be impleaded as three respondents.
06.

In the claim proceedings, the appellant as well as its driver-respondent No. 2-Gurmeet Singh absented despite service to be proceeded ex-parte whereas on behalf of the respondent No.
1-National Insurance Company, a stand came to be taken that insurance policy was a transit policy and was not covering the occupants of the offending car in which the deceased was alleged to be travelling.

07. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pulwama by virtue of award dated 24th August, 2024 came to hold the said three claimants/dependents who are respondents No. 2 to 5 herein entitled to compensation of an amount of Rs. 17, 10,000/- with liability to pay the said compensation being fastened exclusively upon the appellant/ applicant absolving the respondent No. 1-National Insurance Company and also the respondent No. 2- Gurmeet Singh (driver).

08. It is against this award that present time barred appeal is sought to be maintained by the appellant/applicant under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being afflicted by delay of 278 days.

09. Application CM No 5725/2025 by the appellant/applicant is for condonation of delay with the reason cited that the General Manager of the time attending the affairs of appellant/applicant including the case related matter was negligent in discharging his duties and, thus, left the appellant/applicant burdened with liability without it being in actual notice of the case as well as outcome thereof.

10. In the memo of appeal, the impugned award is being challenged on number of grounds but the primary ground is giving of relievement to the respondent No. 1-National Insurance Company from its liability of indemnifying the appellant/applicant in terms of the liability envisaged under the impugned award and to this extent the respondents No. 3 to 5 may not have anything to be concerned about.

11. It appears that the claimants i.e. respondents No. 3 to 5 have reconciled with the quantum of the compensation awarded in their favour and that is why they have gone for execution of the award before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pulwama in which an order dated 14th August, 2025 has come to be passed wherein the appellant/applicant as being the judgment debtor came to be directed to deposit 25% of the principal amount of the award before the Tribunal and to that effect an amount of Rs. 4,27,500/- came to be deposited before coming in the present matter before this Court through the time barred appeal.
12. Notice in CM No. 5724/2025 only to respondent No. 1/non-applicant No. 1- National Insurance Company.
13. Notice in CM No. 5725/2025 also to respondent No. 1/non-applicant No. 1-National Insurance Company.
Peaks Auto Pvt. Ltd Through Its vs National Insurance Company Through Its on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165160875/
2
14. Appellant/applicant to furnish registered postal cover within a period of seven days, whereupon notice shall go to the respondent/non-applicant No. 1-National Insurance Company only.
15. In the meantime, let appellant/applicant deposit amount of Rs. 5, 72,500/- so as to make total advance payment of the award amount to Rs. 10,00,000/- with Rs. 4,27,500/- already deposited.

16. Let this amount of Rs. 5,72,500/- be deposited with the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Pulwama by the appellant/applicant by or before 22nd September, 2025, upon deposit of which the said amount can be released by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pulwama in favour of the respondents No. 3 to 5 /claimants in accordance with the original mandate of the impugned award.
17. Further proceedings in the execution before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pulwama shall come to stay.

18. Send for the record of File No. 07/CP titled "Mst Noor Begum and O rs. vs. Gurmeet Singh and Ors." from the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pulwama.
19.
